title: A versatile and stable reporter platform for human rhinovirus and other enteroviruses
abstract: ABSTRACT Human rhinovirus (HRV), a major cause of upper respiratory infections, has increasingly been associated with lower respiratory tract disease. Although tools to investigate HRV pathogenesis are needed, they remain limited. Reporter viruses expressing fluorescent or luminescent proteins are powerful tools for analyzing viral distribution and replication; however, insertion of a reporter gene often impairs viral replication, and the inserted gene is readily lost during serial passage. To address these problems, we established a versatile and stable strategy for generating reporter HRV and other enteroviruses. The gene encoding mScarlet3, a red fluorescent protein, was inserted between the 5′UTR and VP4 gene, a site previously used in other enteroviruses but not in HRV. Optimizing the 2A cleavage sequence between mScarlet3 and VP4 yielded a reporter HRV with growth kinetics comparable to those of the wild-type virus. To improve the genetic stability of the reporter insert, we evaluated GC-content optimization of the reporter gene and relocation of the cis-acting replication element (CRE). GC-content optimization substantially improved reporter stability in both HRV-B14 and EV-A71, whereas CRE relocation provided additional stabilization in EV-A71 but not in HRV-B14, demonstrating the potential applicability of this strategy to other enteroviruses. This strategy for constructing stable reporter HRV and other enteroviruses will facilitate studies of enterovirus pathogenesis. IMPORTANCE Human rhinovirus (HRV) has lacked a reporter system expressing widely used reporter proteins, such as GFP, that enables visualization of viral dynamics in infected cells and tissues. The only reporter HRV reported to date loses fluorescence upon fixation and tolerates only small inserts, limiting its utility. Meanwhile, the clinical importance of HRV has become increasingly recognized, as reflected by its high detection rate among hospitalized children and recent outbreaks associated with fatal cases. A versatile and stable strategy for constructing reporter HRV is therefore urgently needed. Here, we overcome the two major obstacles to generating stable reporter HRV - impaired viral replication and loss of the inserted gene - and demonstrate that this strategy is also applicable to other enteroviruses. By providing a broadly applicable framework for constructing stable reporter viruses, this work establishes a foundation for visualizing infection dynamics and studying the pathogenesis of HRV and other enteroviruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human rhinovirus (HRV) has increasingly been associated with lower respiratory tract disease, yet tools to investigate HRV pathogenesis remain limited. The lack of a robust reporter system for HRV has hindered the visualization of viral dynamics in infected cells and tissues.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study aimed to address the limitations of existing reporter systems by developing a versatile and stable strategy for generating reporter HRV and other enteroviruses. This strategy was evaluated for its applicability to HRV-B14 and EV-A71, which are representative of non-polio human enteroviruses.
analysis.methods: To improve the genetic stability of the reporter insert, the researchers evaluated GC-content optimization of the reporter gene and relocation of the cis-acting replication element (CRE). They inserted the mScarlet3 gene between the 5′UTR and VP4 gene, optimizing the 2A cleavage sequence to ensure viral replication was not impaired.
analysis.main_results: GC-content optimization substantially improved reporter stability in both HRV-B14 and EV-A71. CRE relocation provided additional stabilization in EV-A71 but not in HRV-B14, demonstrating the potential applicability of this strategy to other enteroviruses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as demonstrating a successful strategy to overcome the two major obstacles to generating stable reporter HRV - impaired viral replication and loss of the inserted gene. This approach provides a broadly applicable framework for constructing stable reporter viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This strategy for constructing stable reporter HRV and other enteroviruses will facilitate studies of enterovirus pathogenesis, offering new insights into viral dynamics and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study does not report limitations, but the evidence is based on direct observations of reporter stability and growth kinetics, which are comparable to those of the wild-type virus. The findings are supported by target-specific methods and results.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a versatile and stable reporter platform for human rhinovirus (HRV) and other enteroviruses, addressing the limitations of existing reporter systems. The researchers inserted a red fluorescent protein gene (mScarlet3) between the 5′UTR and VP4 gene of HRV-B14 and EV-A71, optimizing the 2A cleavage sequence to maintain viral replication. GC-content optimization improved reporter stability in both viruses, while CRE relocation enhanced stability in EV-A71 but not HRV-B14. The strategy enables visualization of viral dynamics in infected cells and tissues, offering new tools for studying enterovirus pathogenesis. The findings are based on direct observations of reporter stability and growth kinetics, demonstrating the potential applicability of this method to other enteroviruses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人鼻病毒 (HRV) 与下呼吸道疾病的关联性日益增强,但研究 HRV 发病机制 的工具仍然有限。由于缺乏强大的 HRV 报告系统,阻碍了受感染细胞和组织中病毒动态的可视化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究旨在通过开发一种通用且稳定的策略来生成报告 HRV 和其他肠道病毒,从而解决现有报告系统的局限性。该策略针对 HRV-B14 和 EV-A71(代表非脊髓灰质炎 人肠道病毒)的适用性进行了评估。
elements_zh.methods: 为了提高报告基因插入片段的遗传稳定性,研究人员评估了报告基因的GC含量优化和顺式作用复制元件(CRE)的重新定位。他们将 mScarlet3 基因插入到 5'UTR 和 VP4 基因之间,优化 2A 切割序列以确保病毒复制不受影响。
elements_zh.main_results: GC 含量优化显着提高了 HRV-B14 和 EV-A71 中报告基因的稳定性。CRE 重定位在 EV-A71 中提供了额外的稳定性,但在 HRV-B14 中没有,这表明该策略对其他肠道病毒的潜在适用性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为证明了一种成功的策略,可以克服产生稳定报告 HRV 的两个主要障碍——病毒复制受损和插入基因丢失。这种方法为构建稳定的报告病毒提供了广泛适用的框架。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这种构建稳定的报告 HRV 和其他肠道病毒的策略将促进肠道病毒 发病机制 的研究,为病毒动力学和潜在治疗靶点提供新的见解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究没有报告局限性,但证据是基于对报告者稳定性和生长动力学的直接观察,这些结果与野生型病毒相当。这些发现得到了针对具体目标的方法和结果的支持。

title_zh: 用于人类鼻病毒和其他肠道病毒的多功能且稳定的报告平台
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human rhinovirus (HRV), a major cause of upper respiratory infections, has increasingly been associated with lower respiratory tract disease. Although tools to investigate HRV pathogenesis are needed, they remain limited. Reporter viruses expressing fluorescent or luminescent proteins are powerful tools for analyzing viral distribution and replication; however, insertion of a reporter gene often impairs viral replication, and the inserted gene is readily lost during serial passage. To address these problems, we established a versatile and stable strategy for generating reporter HRV and other enteroviruses. The gene encoding mScarlet3, a red fluorescent protein, was inserted between the 5′UTR and VP4 gene, a site previously used in other enteroviruses but not in HRV. Optimizing the 2A cleavage sequence between mScarlet3 and VP4 yielded a reporter HRV with growth kinetics comparable to those of the wild-type virus. To improve the genetic stability of the reporter insert, we evaluated GC-content optimization of the reporter gene and relocation of the cis-acting replication element (CRE). GC-content optimization substantially improved reporter stability in both HRV-B14 and EV-A71, whereas CRE relocation provided additional stabilization in EV-A71 but not in HRV-B14, demonstrating the potential applicability of this strategy to other enteroviruses. This strategy for constructing stable reporter HRV and other enteroviruses will facilitate studies of enterovirus pathogenesis. IMPORTANCE Human rhinovirus (HRV) has lacked a reporter system expressing widely used reporter proteins, such as GFP, that enables visualization of viral dynamics in infected cells and tissues. The only reporter HRV reported to date loses fluorescence upon fixation and tolerates only small inserts, limiting its utility. Meanwhile, the clinical importance of HRV has become increasingly recognized, as reflected by its high detection rate among hospitalized children and recent outbreaks associated with fatal cases. A versatile and stable strategy for constructing reporter HRV is therefore urgently needed. Here, we overcome the two major obstacles to generating stable reporter HRV - impaired viral replication and loss of the inserted gene - and demonstrate that this strategy is also applicable to other enteroviruses. By providing a broadly applicable framework for constructing stable reporter viruses, this work establishes a foundation for visualizing infection dynamics and studying the pathogenesis of HRV and other enteroviruses.
abstract_zh: 摘要 人鼻病毒(HRV)是上呼吸道感染的主要原因,但与下呼吸道疾病的关系日益密切。尽管需要研究 HRV 发病机制 的工具,但它们仍然有限。表达荧光或发光蛋白的报告病毒是分析病毒分布和复制的强大工具;然而,报告基因的插入通常会损害病毒复制,并且插入的基因在连续传代过程中很容易丢失。为了解决这些问题,我们建立了一种通用且稳定的策略来生成报告 HRV 和其他肠道病毒。编码 mScarlet3(一种红色荧光蛋白)的基因被插入到 5'UTR 和 VP4 基因之间,该位点以前在其他肠道病毒中使用过,但在 HRV 中没有使用。优化 mScarlet3 和 VP4 之间的 2A 裂解序列产生了报告 HRV,其生长动力学与野生型病毒相当。为了提高报告基因插入的遗传稳定性,我们评估了报告基因的GC含量优化和顺式作用复制元件(CRE)的重新定位。GC 内容优化显着提高了 HRV-B14 和 EV-A71 中报告基因的稳定性,而 CRE 重定位在 EV-A71 中提供了额外的稳定性,但在 HRV-B14 中没有,这表明该策略对其他肠道病毒的潜在适用性。这种构建稳定的报告HRV和其他肠道病毒的策略将有助于肠道病毒发病机制的研究。重要性 人类鼻病毒 (HRV) 缺乏表达广泛使用的报告蛋白(例如 GFP)的报告系统,该系统能够使受感染细胞和组织中的病毒动态可视化。迄今为止报道的唯一的 HRV 报告基因在固定后会失去荧光,并且只能耐受小的插入物,从而限制了其实用性。与此同时,HRV 的临床重要性已得到越来越多的认识,这体现在住院儿童中 HRV 的高检出率以及最近与死亡病例相关的 暴发 上。因此,迫切需要一种通用且稳定的策略来构建记者 HRV。在这里,我们克服了生成稳定报告 HRV 的两个主要障碍 - 病毒复制受损和插入基因丢失 - 并证明该策略也适用于其他肠道病毒。通过为构建稳定的报告病毒提供广泛适用的框架,这项工作为可视化感染动态和研究 HRV 和其他肠道病毒的 发病机制 奠定了基础。

title: Complement-related gene polymorphisms and severity of Coxsackievirus A6-induced hand, foot, and mouth disease in chinese han children: a candidate-gene association study
abstract: Severe hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) remains an important threat to child health. Host genetic factors, particularly those involved in complement activation, may contribute to HFMD susceptibility, but the role of complement-related gene polymorphisms in disease severity remains unclear. We enrolled 189 children with Coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6)-induced HFMD from Henan Children’s Hospital, including 94 severe and 95 mild cases. Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes using a modified phenol-chloroform method, and SNP genotyping was performed by PCR-RFLP. Crude and multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age group and sex were used to evaluate associations between SNP genotypes and severe HFMD. In models adjusted for age group and sex, nominal associations with severe CVA6-induced HFMD were observed for C5 rs3761847 GA versus GG (adjusted OR = 2.523, 95% CI: 1.036–6.143), C3 rs2250656 TC versus TT (adjusted OR = 1.982, 95% CI: 1.061–3.704), and CFH rs1065489 TT versus GG (adjusted OR = 3.125, 95% CI: 1.249–7.818) and GT versus GG (adjusted OR = 2.499, 95% CI: 1.118–5.588). However, none of these associations remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction for multiple testing. The combined SNP model showed limited discriminatory performance, with an apparent AUC of 0.653 and a bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC of 0.631. Exploratory genotype-related differences were also observed in selected laboratory parameters. C5, C3, and CFH variants showed nominal associations with severe CVA6-induced HFMD in this exploratory candidate-gene study, but these findings did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Further validation in larger independent cohorts is required.

title_zh: 中国汉族儿童柯萨奇病毒A6所致手足口病补体相关基因多态性与严重程度的候选基因关联研究
source_body_en: Severe hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) remains an important threat to child health. Host genetic factors, particularly those involved in complement activation, may contribute to HFMD susceptibility, but the role of complement-related gene polymorphisms in disease severity remains unclear. We enrolled 189 children with Coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6)-induced HFMD from Henan Children’s Hospital, including 94 severe and 95 mild cases. Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes using a modified phenol-chloroform method, and SNP genotyping was performed by PCR-RFLP. Crude and multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age group and sex were used to evaluate associations between SNP genotypes and severe HFMD. In models adjusted for age group and sex, nominal associations with severe CVA6-induced HFMD were observed for C5 rs3761847 GA versus GG (adjusted OR = 2.523, 95% CI: 1.036–6.143), C3 rs2250656 TC versus TT (adjusted OR = 1.982, 95% CI: 1.061–3.704), and CFH rs1065489 TT versus GG (adjusted OR = 3.125, 95% CI: 1.249–7.818) and GT versus GG (adjusted OR = 2.499, 95% CI: 1.118–5.588). However, none of these associations remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction for multiple testing. The combined SNP model showed limited discriminatory performance, with an apparent AUC of 0.653 and a bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC of 0.631. Exploratory genotype-related differences were also observed in selected laboratory parameters. C5, C3, and CFH variants showed nominal associations with severe CVA6-induced HFMD in this exploratory candidate-gene study, but these findings did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Further validation in larger independent cohorts is required.

title: Virological and epidemiological investigations of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak, Vietnam, 2023
abstract: We report on the virological and epidemiological features of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak in Vietnam in 2023. Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) subgenogroup B5, first emerging around November 2022, and imported into Vietnam through a single introduction, was the primary cause. Convalescent plasma collected from patients infected with subgenogroups B5 in 2014 and 2023 could neutralize both contemporary viruses with comparable titers, suggesting no evidence of immune evasion. However, at one and six months before the start of the outbreak, only 6.7% of 0- < 3 year-old children in Ho Chi Minh City, an epicenter of the outbreak, had neutralizing antibodies against EV-A71. Seroprevalence increased as the outbreak progressed, coinciding with a drop in EV-A71 infected patients residing in Ho Chi Minh City, suggesting that serosurveillance could be a useful tool to assess the risk of pathogen emergence. Our collective findings have provided novel insights into the epidemiological factors driving EV-A71 emergence, and therefore would inform outbreak preparedness and response, and in particular the development of serosurveillance-based approach to assess the risk of pathogen emergence. EV-A71 infection represents an ongoing public health threat, currently affecting countries in the Asia-Pacific region, but with a high potential to become a global problem, and therefore should be closely monitored.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the virological and epidemiological features of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak in Vietnam in 2023, focusing on Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) subgenogroup B5. The research aimed to understand the factors driving the emergence of EV-A71 and its impact on public health. The study found that only 6.7% of children aged 0-< 3 years in Ho Chi Minh City had neutralizing antibodies against EV-A71 prior to the outbreak. As the outbreak progressed, seroprevalence increased, coinciding with a decline in EV-A71 infections, suggesting that serosurveillance could be a valuable tool for assessing pathogen emergence risk. The findings highlight the need for ongoing monitoring of EV-A71, especially in the Asia-Pacific region, due to its potential to become a global health issue. The study's evidence is based on seroprevalence data and neutralization assays, which provide insights into immune responses and outbreak dynamics. However, the study's scope is limited to a specific geographic area and time period, which may affect the generalizability of its conclusions.

title_zh: 2023 年越南严重 手足口病 暴发 的病毒学和流行病学调查
source_body_en: We report on the virological and epidemiological features of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak in Vietnam in 2023. Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) subgenogroup B5, first emerging around November 2022, and imported into Vietnam through a single introduction, was the primary cause. Convalescent plasma collected from patients infected with subgenogroups B5 in 2014 and 2023 could neutralize both contemporary viruses with comparable titers, suggesting no evidence of immune evasion. However, at one and six months before the start of the outbreak, only 6.7% of 0- < 3 year-old children in Ho Chi Minh City, an epicenter of the outbreak, had neutralizing antibodies against EV-A71. Seroprevalence increased as the outbreak progressed, coinciding with a drop in EV-A71 infected patients residing in Ho Chi Minh City, suggesting that serosurveillance could be a useful tool to assess the risk of pathogen emergence. Our collective findings have provided novel insights into the epidemiological factors driving EV-A71 emergence, and therefore would inform outbreak preparedness and response, and in particular the development of serosurveillance-based approach to assess the risk of pathogen emergence. EV-A71 infection represents an ongoing public health threat, currently affecting countries in the Asia-Pacific region, but with a high potential to become a global problem, and therefore should be closely monitored.

title: Flavaglines as cross-kingdom translation inhibitors: Heavy halides at C6 potentiate antineoplastic, antiviral, and antifungal activities.
abstract: The growing prevalence of cancer, coupled with the rise of multidrug-resistant pathogens, presents a formidable challenge to modern medicine. The flavagline class of secondary metabolites has been shown to possess a unique capacity to target multiple conserved pathways across various human malignancies and microbial pathogens. While numerous structure-activity relationship (SAR) campaigns have established trends with respect to specific indications, cross-kingdom comparative analyses have not been reported to date. In this work, a structurally diverse library comprising 17 novel and 5 natural flavagline analogues, alongside 3 known derivatives, was synthesized and systematically screened for cytotoxicity against five cancer cell lines, inhibition of Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), and activity against multidrug-resistant Candida and Aspergillus pathogens. It was found that introduction of heavy halides (Br or I) at the 6 position significantly potentiates the in vitro biological activities of all tested flavagline chemotypes. Immunoblotting experiments, circumstantial evidence, and molecular docking suggest that the enhanced activity of C6-Br derivatives is consistent with enhanced DEAD-box helicase (eIF4A or DDX3)-RNA clamping. Additionally, the putative flavagline biogenetic precursor chemotypes, aglains and flavonols, were shown to exhibit significant antiviral and antifungal activities. This is the first systematic SAR study directly comparing the anticancer and antipathogenic activities of flavagline derivatives, or any other known translation inhibitors.

title_zh: 黄黄素作为跨界翻译抑制剂:C6 处的重卤化物可增强抗肿瘤、抗病毒药物 和抗真菌活性。
source_body_en: The growing prevalence of cancer, coupled with the rise of multidrug-resistant pathogens, presents a formidable challenge to modern medicine. The flavagline class of secondary metabolites has been shown to possess a unique capacity to target multiple conserved pathways across various human malignancies and microbial pathogens. While numerous structure-activity relationship (SAR) campaigns have established trends with respect to specific indications, cross-kingdom comparative analyses have not been reported to date. In this work, a structurally diverse library comprising 17 novel and 5 natural flavagline analogues, alongside 3 known derivatives, was synthesized and systematically screened for cytotoxicity against five cancer cell lines, inhibition of Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), and activity against multidrug-resistant Candida and Aspergillus pathogens. It was found that introduction of heavy halides (Br or I) at the 6 position significantly potentiates the in vitro biological activities of all tested flavagline chemotypes. Immunoblotting experiments, circumstantial evidence, and molecular docking suggest that the enhanced activity of C6-Br derivatives is consistent with enhanced DEAD-box helicase (eIF4A or DDX3)-RNA clamping. Additionally, the putative flavagline biogenetic precursor chemotypes, aglains and flavonols, were shown to exhibit significant antiviral and antifungal activities. This is the first systematic SAR study directly comparing the anticancer and antipathogenic activities of flavagline derivatives, or any other known translation inhibitors.
abstract_zh: 癌症的不断增长,加上多重耐药病原体的兴起,对现代医学提出了巨大的挑战。黄黄素类次生代谢物已被证明具有独特的能力,可以靶向多种人类恶性肿瘤和微生物病原体的多个保守途径。虽然许多结构-活动关系(SAR)活动已经确定了特定适应症的趋势,但迄今为止尚未报告跨领域的比较分析。在这项工作中,合成了一个结构多样化的文库,包含 17 种新型和 5 种天然黄黄碱类似物以及 3 种已知衍生物,并系统地筛选了其对 5 种癌细胞系的细胞毒性、对肠道病毒 A71 (EV-A71) 的抑制作用以及对多重耐药念珠菌和曲霉病原体的活性。结果发现,在 6 位引入重卤化物(Br 或 I)可显着增强所有测试的黄黄碱化学型的体外生物活性。免疫印迹实验、间接证据和分子对接表明,C6-Br 衍生物的增强活性与增强的 DEAD-box 解旋酶(eIF4A 或 DDX3)-RNA 钳制一致。此外,假定的黄黄素生物遗传前体化学型、黄酮素和黄酮醇,显示出显着的 抗病毒药物 和抗真菌活性。这是第一个系统的 SAR 研究,直接比较黄黄素衍生物或任何其他已知翻译抑制剂的抗癌和抗病原体活性。

title: Ambient air pollution and meteorological factors associated with hand, foot, and mouth disease risk in Shenzhen, China: a time-series study
abstract: Background In China, hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) persists as a prevalent infectious disease with high transmissibility. Nevertheless, the link between environmental determinants and HFMD incidence has not been fully elucidated. The study assessed associations between air pollution, meteorological conditions, and HFMD incidence in Shenzhen, China, while also evaluating shifts in these associations before and after the Enterovirus 71 vaccine and during the COVID-19 epidemic. Methods Daily data on HFMD cases, air pollutants (such as PM 2.5 , PM 10 , SO 2 , NO 2 , CO, and O 3 ), and meteorological variables (including mean temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed) were collected for the period from 2013 to 2022. Associations were assessed using distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM), accounting for immediate and delayed effects. Results Spearman correlation analysis showed that HFMD was positively correlated with SO2, mean temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed, and negatively with PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, and atmospheric pressure. DLNM models revealed that SO2 and CO both elevated cumulative risk at extremely high concentrations, with SO2 showing delayed effects. However, SO2 unexpectedly displayed protective effects in single-lag analysis. NO2 exhibited a U-shaped risk at extreme concentrations despite an overall decreasing trend. O3 showed dual peaks, with protective effects at extremely high concentrations after lag 1. PM 2.5 and PM 10 showed risk peaks at low concentrations but protective effects at extremely high concentrations. Temperature exhibited a dual-peak risk pattern at extremely low and extremely high temperatures, with extreme heat producing sustained effects and extreme cold shorter-lived risk. HFMD risk increased under conditions of extremely high humidity. In general, the risk associated with atmospheric pressure rose as pressure levels increased, and asymmetric lagged effects were observed at both low- and high-concentration extremes. Extremely high wind speed causing short-term harm and extremely low wind speed leading to delayed cumulative risk. Conclusion Meteorological factors exhibit more consistent associations than air pollutants. Mean temperature showed a dual-peak distribution with persistent effects from high temperatures, while atmospheric pressure presented long-lasting impacts of low pressure. There is a positive correlation between relative humidity and the incidence of HFMD. Air pollutants showed inconsistent associations with HFMD. These findings support targeted public health interventions for meteorological factors.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the associations between ambient air pollution and meteorological factors and the risk of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) in Shenzhen, China, with a focus on understanding how these relationships may have changed over time due to public health interventions such as the Enterovirus 71 vaccine and the COVID-19 epidemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This time-series study analyzed daily data on HFMD cases and environmental factors from 2013 to 2022 in Shenzhen, China, encompassing a wide range of pollutants and meteorological variables. The study included both air pollution and meteorological data as key components of the analysis.
analysis.methods: The study employed distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM) to assess the associations between air pollutants, meteorological conditions, and HFMD incidence, accounting for both immediate and delayed effects. Spearman correlation analysis was also used to evaluate the relationships between HFMD and various environmental factors.
analysis.main_results: Spearman correlation analysis showed that HFMD was positively correlated with SO2, mean temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed, and negatively correlated with PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, and atmospheric pressure. DLNM models revealed that SO2 and CO both elevated cumulative risk at extremely high concentrations, with SO2 showing delayed effects. NO2 exhibited a U-shaped risk at extreme concentrations despite an overall decreasing trend. O3 showed dual peaks, with protective effects at extremely high concentrations after lag 1. PM2.5 and PM10 showed risk peaks at low concentrations but protective effects at extremely high concentrations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that meteorological factors exhibited more consistent associations with HFMD than air pollutants, highlighting the need for further research into the complex interactions between environmental variables and disease transmission. The study's novelty lies in its comprehensive evaluation of these associations over time, incorporating changes due to public health interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support targeted public health interventions for meteorological factors that may influence HFMD risk, potentially informing strategies for disease surveillance and prevention in Shenzhen and similar urban settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited by its reliance on observational data, which may introduce confounding factors. The confidence in the findings is moderate due to the complexity of environmental-disease interactions and the potential for unmeasured variables to affect the results.

analysis.summary_en: This time-series study in Shenzhen, China, investigated the associations between ambient air pollution and meteorological factors and the risk of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD). The research aimed to understand how these relationships may have evolved over time due to public health interventions such as the Enterovirus 71 vaccine and the COVID-19 epidemic. Using Spearman correlation and distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM), the study found that HFMD was positively correlated with SO2, mean temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed, while it was negatively correlated with PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, and atmospheric pressure. DLNM models revealed that SO2 and CO elevated risk at extremely high concentrations, with delayed effects for SO2. NO2 showed a U-shaped risk pattern, O3 had dual peaks with protective effects at high concentrations after lag 1, and PM2.5 and PM10 demonstrated risk peaks at low concentrations but protective effects at extremely high concentrations. Temperature and atmospheric pressure also showed complex, non-linear relationships with HFMD risk. The authors concluded that meteorological factors had more consistent associations with HFMD than air pollutants, suggesting the need for targeted public health interventions based on these findings. However, the study's observational design and potential confounding factors limit the confidence in the results, leading to a moderate assessment of evidence strength.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,与空气污染物相比,气象因素与手足口病的关联性更强,这凸显了需要进一步研究环境变量与疾病之间复杂的相互作用。该研究的新颖之处在于它随着时间的推移对这些关联进行了全面评估,纳入了公共卫生干预措施造成的变化。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持对可能影响手足口病风险的气象因素进行有针对性的公共卫生干预,可能为深圳和类似城市环境的疾病 监测 和预防策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据因其对观察数据的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入混杂因素。由于环境与疾病相互作用的复杂性以及未测量的变量可能影响结果,因此研究结果的可信度为中等。

title_zh: 中国深圳环境空气污染和气象因素与手足口病风险的相关性:一项时间序列研究
source_body_en: Background In China, hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) persists as a prevalent infectious disease with high transmissibility. Nevertheless, the link between environmental determinants and HFMD incidence has not been fully elucidated. The study assessed associations between air pollution, meteorological conditions, and HFMD incidence in Shenzhen, China, while also evaluating shifts in these associations before and after the Enterovirus 71 vaccine and during the COVID-19 epidemic. Methods Daily data on HFMD cases, air pollutants (such as PM 2.5 , PM 10 , SO 2 , NO 2 , CO, and O 3 ), and meteorological variables (including mean temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed) were collected for the period from 2013 to 2022. Associations were assessed using distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM), accounting for immediate and delayed effects. Results Spearman correlation analysis showed that HFMD was positively correlated with SO2, mean temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed, and negatively with PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, and atmospheric pressure. DLNM models revealed that SO2 and CO both elevated cumulative risk at extremely high concentrations, with SO2 showing delayed effects. However, SO2 unexpectedly displayed protective effects in single-lag analysis. NO2 exhibited a U-shaped risk at extreme concentrations despite an overall decreasing trend. O3 showed dual peaks, with protective effects at extremely high concentrations after lag 1. PM 2.5 and PM 10 showed risk peaks at low concentrations but protective effects at extremely high concentrations. Temperature exhibited a dual-peak risk pattern at extremely low and extremely high temperatures, with extreme heat producing sustained effects and extreme cold shorter-lived risk. HFMD risk increased under conditions of extremely high humidity. In general, the risk associated with atmospheric pressure rose as pressure levels increased, and asymmetric lagged effects were observed at both low- and high-concentration extremes. Extremely high wind speed causing short-term harm and extremely low wind speed leading to delayed cumulative risk. Conclusion Meteorological factors exhibit more consistent associations than air pollutants. Mean temperature showed a dual-peak distribution with persistent effects from high temperatures, while atmospheric pressure presented long-lasting impacts of low pressure. There is a positive correlation between relative humidity and the incidence of HFMD. Air pollutants showed inconsistent associations with HFMD. These findings support targeted public health interventions for meteorological factors.
abstract_zh: 背景 在中国,手足口病(HFMD)一直是一种高流行、传染性强的传染病。然而,环境决定因素与手足口病 发病率 之间的联系尚未完全阐明。该研究评估了中国深圳的空气污染、气象条件和手足口病 发病率 之间的关联,同时还评估了肠道病毒 71 疫苗 前后以及 COVID-19 流行期间这些关联的变化。方法收集 2013 年至 2022 年期间手足口病病例、空气污染物(例如 PM 2.5 、PM 10 、SO 2 、NO 2 、CO 和 O 3 )和气象变量(包括平均温度、相对湿度、大气压力和风速)的每日数据。使用分布式滞后非线性模型(DLNM)评估关联性,考虑即时和延迟影响。结果 Spearman相关分析显示,手足口病与SO2、平均气温、相对湿度、风速呈正相关,与PM2.5、PM10、NO2、CO、大气压力呈负相关。DLNM 模型显示,SO2 和 CO 在极高浓度下都会增加累积风险,其中 SO2 显示出延迟效应。然而,SO2 在单滞后分析中出乎意料地显示出保护作用。尽管整体呈下降趋势,但二氧化氮在极端浓度下仍表现出 U 形风险。O3 显示双峰,滞后 1 后在极高浓度下具有保护作用。PM 2.5 和 PM 10 在低浓度下显示风险峰,但在极高浓度下显示保护作用。温度在极低和极高温度下呈现出双峰风险模式,极端高温会产生持续影响,而极端寒冷会产生短期风险。在湿度极高的条件下,手足口病的风险会增加。一般来说,与大气压力相关的风险随着压力水平的增加而增加,并且在低浓度和高浓度极端情况下都观察到不对称滞后效应。极高的风速会造成短期危害,极低的风速会导致延迟累积风险。结论 气象因素比空气污染物表现出更一致的关联。平均温度呈现双峰分布,高温影响持续,而大气压呈现低压长期影响。相对湿度与手足口病的发病率呈正相关。空气污染物与手足口病的关联性不一致。这些发现支持针对气象因素采取有针对性的公共卫生干预措施。

title: Discovery of antivirals against enteroviruses by targeting viral non-structural protein 2C and structural protein VP1
abstract: Enteroviruses (EVs), including EV-D68, EV-A71, and coxsackievirus B3 (CVB3), impose a substantial global disease burden, yet no antiviral therapies are currently approved. In this thesis, we developed two antiviral strategies targeting the highly conserved nonstructural protein 2C and the viral capsid protein VP1. In the first part of the thesis, structure-property relationship (SPR) studies led to the identification of the promising 2C inhibitor Jun6504, which exhibited broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple enterovirus strains and favorable pharmacokinetic properties. In a neonatal mouse model of EV-D68-induced paralysis, Jun6504 demonstrated significant antiviral efficacy. To address the lack of direct biochemical assays for enteroviral 2C inhibitors, we developed a fluorescence polarization (FP)-based binding assay targeting a conserved allosteric pocket in enteroviral 2C proteins, enabling direct and quantitative measurement of inhibitor binding affinity and facilitating target-based inhibitor discovery and optimization. In parallel, structure-based optimization of a virtual screening hit yielded the VP1-targeting inhibitors Jun11695 and Jun11787, which exhibited nanomolar antiviral potency against EV-D68 and micromolar activity against EV-A71 and CVB3. Both inhibitors demonstrated complementary evidence of VP1 target engagement, favorable pharmacokinetic properties, and significant reductions in viral loads and paralysis progression in vivo. To overcome the low genetic barrier to resistance associated with conventional VP1 capsid inhibitors, we further developed Jun15702, a first-in-class VP1-targeting degrader. Jun15702 exhibited potent antiviral activity against multiple wild-type EV-D68 strains and retained submicromolar potency against the recombinant pleconaril-resistant variant rMO-VP1 F159V. Mechanistic studies demonstrated the distinct dual mode-of-action of Jun15702 that not only inhibited viral entry but also induced CRBN-dependent degradation of VP1 when administered after viral entry. Collectively, these studies establish enteroviral 2C and VP1 as therapeutically tractable antiviral targets and provide complementary occupancy-driven and targeted protein degradation strategies for developing next-generation antivirals against enterovirus infections.

source_records.abstract: Enteroviruses (EVs), including EV-D68, EV-A71, and coxsackievirus B3 (CVB3), impose a substantial global disease burden, yet no antiviral therapies are currently approved. In this thesis, we developed two antiviral strategies targeting the highly conserved nonstructural protein 2C and the viral capsid protein VP1. In the first part of the thesis, structure-property relationship (SPR) studies led to the identification of the promising 2C inhibitor Jun6504, which exhibited broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple enterovirus strains and favorable pharmacokinetic properties. In a neonatal mouse model of EV-D68-induced paralysis, Jun6504 demonstrated significant antiviral efficacy. To address the lack of direct biochemical assays for enteroviral 2C inhibitors, we developed a fluorescence polarization (FP)-based binding assay targeting a conserved allosteric pocket in enteroviral 2C proteins, enabling direct and quantitative measurement of inhibitor binding affinity and facilitating target-based inhibitor discovery and optimization. In parallel, structure-based optimization of a virtual screening hit yielded the VP1-targeting inhibitors Jun11695 and Jun11787, which exhibited nanomolar antiviral potency against EV-D68 and micromolar activity against EV-A71 and CVB3. Both inhibitors demonstrated complementary evidence of VP1 target engagement, favorable pharmacokinetic properties, and significant reductions in viral loads and paralysis progression in vivo. To overcome the low genetic barrier to resistance associated with conventional VP1 capsid inhibitors, we further developed Jun15702, a first-in-class VP1-targeting degrader. Jun15702 exhibited potent antiviral activity against multiple wild-type EV-D68 strains and retained submicromolar potency against the recombinant pleconaril-resistant variant rMO-VP1 F159V. Mechanistic studies demonstrated the distinct dual mode-of-action of Jun15702 that not only inhibited viral entry but also induced CRBN-dependent degradation of VP1 when administered after viral entry. Collectively, these studies establish enteroviral 2C and VP1 as therapeutically tractable antiviral targets and provide complementary occupancy-driven and targeted protein degradation strategies for developing next-generation antivirals against enterovirus infections.

abstract_zh: 肠道病毒 (EV),包括 EV-D68、EV-A71 和柯萨奇病毒 B3 (CVB3),给全球带来了巨大的疾病负担,但目前尚无 抗病毒药物 疗法获得批准。在本论文中,我们针对高度保守的非结构蛋白2C和病毒衣壳蛋白VP1开发了两种抗病毒药物策略。在论文的第一部分,结构-性质关系(SPR)研究鉴定出了有前景的2C抑制剂Jun6504,它对多种肠道病毒株表现出广谱抗病毒药物活性和良好的药代动力学特性。在 EV-D68 诱导的瘫痪新生小鼠模型中,Jun6504 表现出显着的 抗病毒药物 功效。为了解决肠道病毒 2C 抑制剂缺乏直接生化检测的问题,我们开发了一种基于荧光偏振 (FP) 的结合检测,针对肠道病毒 2C 蛋白中的保守变构袋,从而能够直接定量测量抑制剂结合亲和力,并促进基于目标的抑制剂发现和优化。与此同时,基于结构的虚拟筛选结果优化产生了 VP1 靶向抑制剂 Jun11695 和 Jun11787,它们对 EV-D68 表现出纳摩尔 抗病毒药物 效力,对 EV-A71 和 CVB3 表现出微摩尔活性。两种抑制剂都证明了 VP1 靶点参与、有利的药代动力学特性以及体内病毒载量和麻痹进展显着减少的互补证据。为了克服与传统 VP1 衣壳抑制剂相关的低遗传耐药性障碍,我们进一步开发了 Jun15702,这是一种一流的 VP1 靶向降解剂。Jun15702 对多种野生型 EV-D68 菌株表现出有效的 抗病毒药物 活性,并保留了对重组普来可那利抗性变体 rMO-VP1 F159V 的亚微摩尔效力。机制研究表明,Jun15702 具有独特的双重作用模式,在病毒进入后给药时,不仅能抑制病毒进入,还能诱导 VP1 依赖于 CRBN 的降解。总的来说,这些研究将肠道病毒 2C 和 VP1 确定为治疗上易于处理的 抗病毒药物 靶点,并为开发下一代抗肠道病毒感染的 抗病毒药物 提供补充的占用驱动和靶向蛋白质降解策略。

title: From eradicating wild poliovirus to eradicating vaccine-derived polioviruses: why oral polio vaccine use must now be ended
abstract: Abstract Wild poliovirus (WPV)2 was eradicated globally in 1999, and WPV3 was eradicated in 2012. Since 2016, endemic transmission of WPV1 has remained restricted to Afghanistan and Pakistan. Circulating vaccine-derived polioviruses (cVDPVs) have become the leading cause of poliovirus transmission and paralytic disease globally. As cVDPVs originate from oral poliovirus vaccine (OPV) strains, the polio endgame must address both cVDPV outbreaks and the mechanism that generates them. We propose defining cVDPV eradication as sustained zero disease, zero transmission, and zero emergence of new cVDPV lineages. Continued OPV use exposes children, predominantly in low- and middle-income countries, to avoidable risks of vaccine-associated paralysis and cVDPV outbreaks. Accelerated transition to inactivated poliovirus vaccine-only schedules and cessation of OPV use are essential for a sustainable and equitable polio endgame.

title: An RT‒qPCR Assay for Rapid Detection of Coxsackievirus A4
abstract: Coxsackievirus A4 (CV-A4) is a major cause of hand, foot, and mouth disease and herpangina in children, and has been linked to severe complications. However, current detection methods, including commercial RT-qPCR kits, suffer from false-negative and false-positive results. This study aimed to develop a sensitive and specific TaqMan-based RT-qPCR assay for the rapid detection of CV-A4, targeting the conserved VP1 region covering genotypes A–D and subgenotypes C1–C5, with emphasis on the predominant C2 subgenotype in China. The assay was evaluated using a panel of enteroviruses, influenza virus, adenovirus, and rhinovirus, and compared with two commercial kits using 82 CV-A4-positive and 100 negative clinical specimens. The established assay demonstrated high specificity with no cross-reactivity, a detection limit of 2.1 TCID50 equivalents/mL, and excellent reproducibility (CV ≤ 3.03%). In clinical testing, it achieved a 100% detection rate (82/82) with no false positives within 1.5 h, outperforming the two commercial kits, which showed positive rates of 91.5% and 89.0%, and false-positive rates of 0% and 1%, respectively. These findings indicate that our RT-qPCR assay offers superior sensitivity and specificity for CV-A4 detection, particularly for the C2 subgenotype, and represents a promising tool for laboratory diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance.

title: A mathematical model for polio eradication considering the impact of booster vaccination and paralysis dynamics
abstract: Poliomyelitis, also known as polio, is a contagious viral illness that predominantly impacts young children, leading to paralysis and, in severe instances, death. Despite worldwide initiatives aimed at elimination, the spread of the poliovirus persists in various areas, highlighting the need for robust vaccination strategies. This research employed a mathematical model to explore the dynamics of poliovirus transmission, integrating vaccination as a crucial method for disease control. The model was analyzed to determine the basic reproduction number [Formula: see text] and the stability properties of the disease-free and endemic equilibrium (EE). Our findings demonstrated that the system achieves local asymptotic stability when the basic reproduction number is less than one, global asymptotic stability when it is exactly one, and maintains a stable EE when it is greater than one. Sensitivity analysis revealed critical parameters influencing the basic reproduction number, emphasizing the impact of vaccination coverage and disease transmission rates on polio dynamics. More so, numerical simulations showed that vaccination coverage of about [Formula: see text] would be enough to eradicate polio from the population.

title: Absence of Nipah virus antibodies and detection of Porcine kobuvirus, Porcine enterovirus-9 and Bocavirus in pigs during a Nipah virus outbreak investigation in West Bengal, India
abstract: The Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly lethal zoonotic virus that causes respiratory disease and encephalitis in humans. Historically, the NiV outbreaks in Malaysia and Singapore (1998–1999) involved domestic pigs as amplifying intermediate hosts, whereas subsequent outbreaks in India and Bangladesh have primarily been attributed to direct bat-to-human transmission or nosocomial spread, with no documented involvement of livestock. The role of intermediate hosts in NiV transmission is less studied. We report findings from a study conducted in West Bengal during the NiV outbreak in January 2026, investigating the role of local pig populations in NiV transmission and screening diseased pigs for other etiologies using metagenomic sequencing. Blood, nasal, rectal, throat and ocular swab samples were collected from 119 domestic pigs in Nadia, Kolkata, North 24 Paraganas, and Purba Bardhaman districts of West Bengal. Virological and serological tests for NiV infection were performed using real-time qRT-PCR and swine IgG ELISA. A subset of nasal and rectal swab samples from diseased pigs also underwent metagenomic sequencing. All swab samples tested negative for NiV RNA, and no antibodies were found in the serum samples. Metagenomic sequencing detected genomes of Porcine Kobuvirus (PKV) and Porcine enterovirus 9 (PEV9), prevalent in the Indian pig population as well as Porcine Bocavirus (PBoV), adding to the limited molecular reports of PBoV from India. The serological and virological investigation conducted in 119 pigs from West Bengal revealed no evidence of NiV infection. The detection of other prevalent porcine viruses and PBoV, a relatively infrequently reported virus from India, emphasizes the need for genomic surveillance and incorporation of the One Health concept into disease surveillance.

full_text: Nature Reviews Microbiology nature reviews microbiology https://doi.org/10.1038/s41579-026-01372-1 Review article Check for updates Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses Hendrik Jan Thibaut 1, Dirk Jochmans 1,3, Christophe Van Dijck2,3, Manon Laporte 1,3, Laurens Liesenborghs 2 & Johan Neyts1 Abstract Small molecule antiviral drugs have transformed the management of infections such as those caused by HIV, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, herpesviruses and influenza viruses. Effective antiviral therapeutics remain unavailable for many other often life-threatening viral infections, many of which are caused by RNA viruses. The development of potent, safe and orally available antivirals is therefore essential both to address current unmet medical needs and to strengthen epidemic and pandemic preparedness. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for building a diversified portfolio of broader-spectrum antivirals against RNA viruses with activity spanning multiple genera, entire families or even crossing viral families. We provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved and investigational antiviral agents active against RNA viruses and discuss the biological determinants that underlie their antiviral spectrum. Finally, we outline the clinical development frameworks required to accelerate the evaluation of such drugs, in particular in the context of outbreaks. Sections Introduction One drug to treat them all? Direct-acting antivirals versus host-targeting antivirals New approaches to discover new targets for broader-acting antivirals Translational readiness Conclusions 1KU Leuven Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Transplantation, Antiviral Drug and Vaccine Research Group, Leuven, Belgium. 2Department of Clinical Sciences, Institute of Tropical Medicine, Antwerp, Belgium. 3These authors contributed equally: Dirk Jochmans, Christophe Van Dijck, Manon Laporte. e-mail: johan.neyts@kuleuven.be Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article Alongside vaccine development, sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery is therefore essential. Antiviral drug development has so far largely been focused on viral infections that offer large and predict- able commercial markets (for example, those caused by HIV and HCV). It is obviously unrealistic and economically unsustainable to develop specific antiviral drugs for each known viral pathogen. Newly emerging viruses will most likely belong to viral families already known (Table 1) today. Advances in metagenomics and high-throughput sequencing greatly expanded our understanding of viral diversity, and although new viral families may still be discovered, such events are becoming increasingly rare. Together, this strongly supports a strategy in which broader-acting small molecule antiviral (BSA) drugs are developed. Such drugs can be used for the treatment and prophylaxis of infec- tions with known viruses for which no antiviral treatment is available and, in the case of epidemics or pandemics, as a rapid response option while other countermeasures, such as vaccines and mAbs, are being developed12,13. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for the development of BSAs and provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved or experi- mental antiviral drugs active against viruses with an RNA genome. We also outline strategies for target discovery and accelerated clinical development. One drug to treat them all? The term ‘broad-spectrum’ antiviral has been widely used but lacks, to the best of our knowledge, a clear definition. Here, we propose instead to use the term ‘broader-spectrum’ antivirals and distinguish three categories: (i) cross-family BSAs with activity across unrelated viral families within or across a certain genome architecture, that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA); (ii) pan-family BSAs that act across the different genera of a given viral family (for example, pan-paramyxovirus drugs); and (iii) intra-family BSAs, which are active against multiple serotypes and genotypes of a particular virus (for example, pan-serotype dengue virus (DENV) Introduction Viruses, whether known or yet to emerge (‘virus X’), remain a major threat to global health. Vaccines, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and antiviral drugs are each important and complementary in controlling viral infections. Vaccination has led to the eradication of smallpox, brought polio close to eradication and massively reduced disease and mortality associated with numerous viral infections, such as measles virus, mumps virus, rubella virus, influenza virus, severe acute respira- tory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human papillomavirus1–3. For several important human pathogens, such as HIV, hepatitis C virus (HCV), herpes simplex viruses (HSV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), rhinoviruses and many others, the devel- opment of highly effective vaccines has proved difficult or remains elusive, often despite decades of intensive effort. They generally have an excellent safety profile and can be highly effective, although they require injections, are virus specific or variant spe- cific and can rapidly select for escape variants8,9. Like vaccines, mAbs can be developed only once a new pathogen has been identified and characterized. By contrast, small molecule antiviral drugs offer several distinct advantages. They can be administered orally and have the potential to cover a broader spectrum of viruses (Box 1) than vaccines and mAbs. Antiviral drugs have revolutionized the treatment of certain (chronic) viral infections such as those caused by either HIV, HBV, HCV, HSV-1 and HSV-2, and CMV. More recently, antiviral drugs have also become availa- ble against some other viruses including influenza viruses, SARS-CoV-2 and hepatitis delta virus. However, for the majority of the more than 200 known human pathogenic viruses, no antiviral drugs are available. Most of these viruses are RNA viruses — the focus of this Review — including many emerging and clinically important pathogens10–12. For example, remdesivir, a nucleoside viral polymerase inhibitor, is active against viruses belonging to different viral families, that is, the (−)ssRNA Filoviridae, Paramyxoviridae, Pneumoviridae and Arenaviridae as well as the (+) ssRNA Flaviviridae, Picornaviridae and Coronaviridae. Examples include neuraminidase inhibitors such as oseltamivir, zanamivir and peramivir that are active against both influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae). Nirmatrelvir is a reversible covalent, peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor that inhibits human and animal coronaviruses belonging to different genera within the family Coronaviridae. Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article inhibitors) or active against one or more (but not all) genera of a viral family (Box 1). The need for broader-acting antivirals and their desired spectrum of activity are mostly defined by the particular (clinical) context (Boxes 2 and 3). For viruses that cause a high number of annual cases (for example, RSV), there might be a sufficiently large market, and thus incentives, to develop virus-specific drugs. Conversely, there might be no or less financial incentive to develop virus-specific drugs for viruses that cause a rather limited number of cases but that col- lectively, within their genus or family, are responsible for a substan- tial clinical burden (for example, coxsackieviruses and echoviruses, EV-D68 and EV-A71 that all belong to the genus Enterovirus). In this case, the development of antivirals that are broadly active across the entire Enterovirus genus (pan-Enterovirus; category intra-family BSAs) represents a more realistic approach. In the context of epidemic or pan- demic preparedness, access to pan-family and cross-family BSAs may be particularly important, as it cannot be predicted which viral family a newly emerging pathogen (‘virus X’) will belong to. Given the extensive genetic diversity and distinct replication strategies of viral families, the development of a single cross-family drug with potent activity against all RNA virus families is likely to be unrealistic. Rather, a more feasible strategy may be to establish a portfolio of different types of BSAs that collectively provide, either alone or in combination, coverage across the RNA virus landscape. title_original: Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the development of broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals (BSAs) against RNA viruses, particularly human enteroviruses, with an emphasis on non-polio enteroviruses such as EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, CV-A16, and echoviruses. The central question is whether BSAs can be developed to target multiple RNA virus genera, families, or even cross families, and how this can address current unmet medical needs and improve pandemic preparedness.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic search methods or meta-analysis. It provides a non-exhaustive overview of approved and investigational antiviral agents active against RNA viruses, including human enteroviruses, and discusses the biological determinants underlying their antiviral spectrum. The authors also outline the clinical development frameworks needed for evaluating such drugs, particularly in outbreak scenarios.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that developing BSAs is a viable strategy to address the limitations of current antiviral therapies for RNA viruses. It highlights the importance of targeting conserved viral components to achieve broad-spectrum activity and emphasizes the need for sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery to meet both current and future medical needs.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while advances in metagenomics and high-throughput sequencing have expanded our understanding of viral diversity, the development of BSAs remains challenging due to the complexity of viral biology and the need for precise targeting. There is a lack of comprehensive data on the efficacy and safety of BSAs in clinical settings, particularly for non-polio human enteroviruses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should prioritize the identification of conserved viral targets and the development of antiviral agents with broad-spectrum activity. It also recommends strengthening clinical development frameworks to enable rapid evaluation of BSAs during outbreaks, especially for viruses like EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, and CV-A16.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the development of broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals (BSAs) against RNA viruses, with a focus on human enteroviruses such as EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, CV-A16, and echoviruses. It argues that creating BSAs is essential to address the lack of effective treatments for many RNA viruses and to improve pandemic preparedness. The review highlights the biological rationale for BSAs, discusses existing antiviral agents, and outlines the need for clinical frameworks to evaluate these drugs. However, it also identifies challenges, including the complexity of viral biology and the absence of robust clinical data. The implications emphasize the importance of targeting conserved viral components and accelerating research and development for BSAs, particularly in outbreak contexts.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the development of broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals (BSAs) against RNA viruses, particularly human enteroviruses, with an emphasis on non-polio enteroviruses such as EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, CV-A16, and echoviruses. The central question is whether BSAs can be developed to target multiple RNA virus genera, families, or even cross families, and how this can address current unmet medical needs and improve pandemic preparedness.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic search methods or meta-analysis. It provides a non-exhaustive overview of approved and investigational antiviral agents active against RNA viruses, including human enteroviruses, and discusses the biological determinants underlying their antiviral spectrum. The authors also outline the clinical development frameworks needed for evaluating such drugs, particularly in outbreak scenarios.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that developing BSAs is a viable strategy to address the limitations of current antiviral therapies for RNA viruses. It highlights the importance of targeting conserved viral components to achieve broad-spectrum activity and emphasizes the need for sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery to meet both current and future medical needs.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while advances in metagenomics and high-throughput sequencing have expanded our understanding of viral diversity, the development of BSAs remains challenging due to the complexity of viral biology and the need for precise targeting. There is a lack of comprehensive data on the efficacy and safety of BSAs in clinical settings, particularly for non-polio human enteroviruses.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should prioritize the identification of conserved viral targets and the development of antiviral agents with broad-spectrum activity. It also recommends strengthening clinical development frameworks to enable rapid evaluation of BSAs during outbreaks, especially for viruses like EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, and CV-A16.

full_text: ABSTRACTEnterovirus 2B is a highly conserved, functionally versatile, nonstructural protein. The classic viroporin model, which restricts its role to ion channel formation, cannot account for its interactions with host factors such as Bcl-2-associated X protein, interleukin enhancer-binding factor 2, and karyopherin subunit alpha 1, nor its functional divergence among enteroviruses. We propose a novel, testable membrane stress sensor hypothesis: the transmembrane helices of 2B sense lipid composition and pH changes, and through conformational dynamics, spatiotemporally coordinate calcium signaling, cell death pathway selection, including apoptosis, pyroptosis, autophagy, and ferroptosis, and immune evasion. We elaborate on this framework across six dimensions: structure–function mapping, calcium signaling, cell death pathways, immune evasion, evolutionary footprint, and antiviral targeting, along with cross-virus comparisons. We highlight key evidence gaps and limitations, and propose several future research directions. This framework establishes a mechanistic foundation for understanding 2B function and guiding rational anti-enteroviral drug designs. Supplementary MaterialSupplementary data.docx Conclusions and outlookThis study proposes an integrative framework in which the enterovirus 2B protein acts as a “membrane stress sensor,” thereby overcoming the limitations of the traditional viroporin model. Through conformational dynamics, the transmembrane helices of 2B sense changes in the membrane microenvironment (lipid composition, pH, and curvature) and coordinate calcium signaling, cell death pathway selection, and immune evasion outputs in a spatiotemporally specific manner. This framework provides a unified explanation for the direct interactions of 2B with host factors such as Bax, NLRP3, and KPNA1, the functional divergence among different viruses, and the evolutionary footprint of the 2B region as a recombination hotspot.Key uncertainties(1) Does 2B exhibit calcium ion selectivity, or does it form a nonselective pore? However, direct evidence from planar lipid bilayer electrophysiology experiments is required. (2) Is the pH dependence of EVD68 2B mediated by a specific histidine residue (e.g. H53)? Site-directed mutagenesis and functional assays under controlled pH conditions are required. (3) The specific molecular mechanism by which 2B blocks autophagosome-lysosome fusion remains to be elucidated. (4) Does 2B degrade WTAP via the calcium–calpain pathway or through another mechanism? Direct verification is required. (5) Direct conformational evidence of 2B in different membrane environments is still lacking, and NMR or cryo-EM studies are required. (6) The membrane stress sensor framework remains a hypothesis. Direct experimental evidence for lipid- or pH-dependent conformational switching of 2B is required to validate or refute this model.A comparative perspective on viroporin biology illuminates both the conserved principles and unique features of 2B. The Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) p7 and influenza M2 viroporins have yielded tractable targets for antiviral drug development: amantadine and rimantadine block M2-mediated proton conductance, while a broad array of alkylated imino-sugar derivatives inhibits p7 channel activity. These precedents validate the viroporin channel as an antiviral druggable target and encourage analogous pharmacological exploration of enterovirus 2B. The membrane stress sensor framework proposed here extends beyond 2B, and similar conformational coupling between the membrane physical properties and channel gating may represent a broader strategy exploited by diverse viroporins. Future structure-guided drug design targeting the 2B gating interface or its lipid-binding determinants may benefit from the lessons learned from the M2 and p7 systems.Future directionsTo validate the membrane stress sensor hypothesis, the following directions are proposed as future priorities: (1) Structural elucidation: Determine the high-resolution structures of 2B in different membrane environments using cryo-EM or solid-state NMR, and directly test the predicted “open” and “closed” states. (2) Verification of conformational dynamics: FRET-based live-cell conformational reporter systems will be developed to monitor real-time conformational changes in 2B during infection. (3) Targeted intervention: Development of small-molecule inhibitors based on the stem-loop hinge region and interaction interfaces, followed by validation of their antiviral efficacy. (4) Pathogenic mechanisms: Elucidate how differences in the membrane environment of 2B in different tissues/cell types determine viral pathogenicity. (5) Cross-virus comparisons: Systematically compare the conformational dynamics and membrane environment responsiveness of 2B proteins from different picornavirus genera to test whether the “membrane stress sensor” concept has a broader applicability. This framework offers a mechanistic basis for anti-enterovirus drug design and may inform studies on other viroporins with similarly broad functional repertoires. IntroductionThe genus Enterovirus within the family Picornaviridae comprises over 250 clinically significant serotypes that circulate worldwide [1–3]. Enterovirus infections manifest with a diverse spectrum of clinical presentations, including upper and lower respiratory tract illnesses, gastroenteritis, hand-foot-and-mouth disease, conjunctivitis, myocarditis, severe neonatal sepsis-like disease, aseptic meningitis, encephalitis, acute flaccid paralysis (AFP), and AFM [3–6]. Important human pathogens within this genus include coxsackieviruses, enterovirus A71 (EVA71), enterovirus D68 (EVD68), echoviruses, and poliovirus (PV) [7–9]. Although these viruses share characteristics such as a small genome, rapid evolution, and broad pathogenic spectrum, targeted antiviral drugs remain absent. The functional pleiotropy of nonstructural protein 2B has emerged as a major obstacle to rational drug design. Understanding how a single ~100-amino-acid protein can engage in such disparate pathways is the central question addressed in this review.Enteroviruses possess a single-stranded, positive-sense RNA genome of approximately 7.5 kb in length [10–12]. A single open reading frame encodes a polyprotein that is proteolytically processed into three precursor regions: P1 (structural proteins VP1–VP4) and non-structural regions P2 and P3 [13]. The 2B protein, together with 2A (protease) [14,15] and 2C (helicase/ATPase) [16–18], constitutes the P2 region of the viral genome. Whereas 2A and 3C perform well-defined enzymatic functions, namely the proteolytic cleavage of viral and host targets [19,20], 2B is remarkable for its broad functional repertoire. Understanding how a single ~100-amino-acid protein can engage in such disparate pathways is the central question addressed in this review.The 2B protein is a non-structural protein of approximately 100 amino acids, encoded by the enterovirus genome [21,22]. Since its discovery in the 1980s, it has been defined as a “viroporin,” a protein that disrupts ion homeostasis by forming transmembrane hydrophilic pores [23–25]. Across viral families, viroporins share conserved strategies of membrane perturbation, including pore formation, lipid bilayer disordering, and membrane curvature sensing, underscoring the evolutionary convergence of these mechanisms [26,27]. Well-characterized examples include HCV p7, influenza A M2, and Human Immunodeficiency Virus type 1 (HIV-1) Vpu, each of which exploits distinct membrane-targeting mechanisms while sharing a common capacity to dysregulate host ion homeostasis [28–31]. The enterovirus 2B protein extends this paradigm with a uniquely dynamic topology that may enable membrane stress sensing. This framework, which has dominated research for three decades, successfully explains the effects of 2B on calcium signaling and membrane permeability during early viral replication. However, intensive research over the past decade has revealed a functional breadth that far exceeds the scope of traditional pore models. Limitations of the viroporin model and the membrane stress sensor hypothesisFirst, the pore model cannot explain the breadth of protein–protein interactions (PPI) in cell membranes. 2B has been shown to directly interacts with multiple host proteins, including Bax [32], NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) [33], Karyopherin subunit alpha 1 (KPNA1) [34], Interleukin enhancer-binding factor 2 (ILF2) [35], Cluster of Differentiation 74 (CD74) [36], Voltage-Dependent Anion Channel 3 (VDAC3) [37], and N-Acetyltransferase 8 (NAT8) [38]. These interactions span apoptosis, inflammation, nuclear transport, and immune recognition, extending far beyond the scope of ion-channel activity.Second, the pore model cannot explain species-specific functional divergence. The stable association of EVD68 2B with the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane depends on an acidic environment; when autophagic flux is blocked and vesicle acidification is insufficient, 2B cannot be stably anchored to the membrane [39], a phenomenon not observed for coxsackievirus B3 (CVB3) or PV. The E40K mutation in CVB3 2B produces a quasi-infectious phenotype that can be rescued by trans-complementation [40], suggesting differences in the functional plasticity among enterovirus 2B proteins. Moreover, the subcellular localization differs: CVB3 2B is primarily localized to the Golgi apparatus, whereas PV 2B exhibits a distinct topological orientation [22,41].Third, the pore model cannot accommodate discrepancies between functional redundancy and pore essentiality. The impact of 2B deletion on viral replication varies considerably among viruses: siRNA-mediated knockdown of EVA71 2B markedly reduces but does not abolish viral replication [42], while a CVB3 2B-derived peptide potently inhibits the virus without achieving sterilizing clearance [43].Fourth, the pore model cannot incorporate post-transcriptional RNA-level regulation, such as N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification of Lon Peptidase 1 (LONP1) mRNA. A direct RNA-modification link between 2B and ferroptosis was established in a recent study [44].In summary, the existing framework can no longer accommodate the functional breadth and depth of 2B. Studies have shown that the transmembrane helices of 2B can respond with conformational sensitivity to physicochemical parameters, such as membrane lipid composition and pH, with distinct conformational states corresponding to different downstream effector outputs, a characteristic that endows 2B with “sensor” functionality. Therefore, this study proposes a new theoretical framework: defining 2B as a membrane stress sensor, whose diverse functional outputs arise from its conformational responsiveness to changes in the membrane microenvironment. This framework comprises three operational criteria.We emphasize that this framework is a testable working hypothesis and not a validated mechanism. Direct experimental evidence for conformational switching under different membrane conditions is currently lacking, and the three operational criteria defined below remain to be experimentally verified.Conformational responsiveness to changes in the membrane microenvironmentThe transmembrane helices (H1/H2) and stem-loop hinge region of 2B adopt different conformational states in different membrane environments. These environmental parameters include lipid composition, membrane curvature, and pH values. These conformational states can be captured using structural biology approaches [e.g. such as fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR)].Distinct conformational states correspond to different functional outputsSpecific conformational states can expose different protein interaction interfaces, thereby selectively activating pathways such as calcium signaling, apoptosis, pyroptosis, and immune evasion. Conformation-locking mutants exhibit directional changes in their functional spectra.Membrane microenvironment is essential for functional switchingThe functional switching of 2B strictly depends on changes in the membrane environmental parameters. For example, differences in lipid composition among the endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondrial, and autophagosomal membranes may directly determine whether 2B activates Bax or NLRP3, and disruption of the pH gradient can lead to 2B degradation or its inactivation.Throughout this review, we distinguished three categories of evidence: (i) experimentally validated: conclusions directly supported by published experimental data, including mutagenesis, co-immunoprecipitation, FRET, and functional assays. (ii) Inferred from indirect evidence: conclusions consistent with the available data but not yet confirmed by direct experimentation. (iii) Speculative: components of the membrane stress sensor hypothesis that generate testable predictions but currently lack experimental support. All speculative statements are explicitly identified in the text.We elaborate on this framework across six dimensions: structure–function mapping, calcium signaling, cell death regulation (encompassing apoptosis, pyroptosis, autophagy, and ferroptosis), immune evasion, evolutionary footprint, and antiviral targeting. Studies using CVB3 2B as a model have shown that the protein contains two hydrophobic transmembrane regions (H1 and H2) connected by a hydrophilic stem loop, forming a typical class IIA viroporin topology [23,24,41]. H1 mediates insertion into the ER membrane, whereas H2 participates in oligomerization to form tetrameric pores. A single point mutation, V56A (located in the stem loop), completely abolishes the ability to induce autophagy, indicating that this region is crucial for conformational stability [45]. Mutational analysis and mammalian two-hybrid experiments further confirmed that the stem-loop region of 2B (particularly the58 RNHDD62 motif) is essential for its multimerization and membrane permeabilization activities [46,47].However, the topological types of these viruses differ. PV 2B and EVA71 2B adopt a type IIB topology (both N- and C-termini facing the cytosol), whereas CVB3 2B adopts a type IIA topology (both termini facing the lumen) [23,48]. This topological difference may affect accessibility to different host factors and represents a structural basis for the functional divergence.
