full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionWastewater metagenomic alpha diversity exhibited variation across the three sampling years. Samples were collected in July 2024, June 2025, and March 2026; therefore, sampling year was intrinsically linked to sampling month and season in this study. The composition of sampling sites also varied across years: Hezuo and Zhangye were each represented by two samples in 2024 and 2025, respectively, whereas Dingxi was included only in 2026. Statistical analysis revealed a significant negative correlation between the Simpson index and sampling year, whereas the Shannon index showed a negative but nonsignificant correlation, suggesting that the two diversity metrics captured different aspects of community variation. Overall, the observed changes in alpha diversity may reflect the combined effects of annual, seasonal, and spatial factors. Environmental conditions may have contributed to these between-year differences. Previous research on influent wastewater bacterial communities has demonstrated seasonal structuring associated primarily with wastewater temperature and, in some settings, with precipitation, wastewater flow, and physicochemical variables (LaMartina et al., 2021). These variables should therefore be regarded as plausible confounders of the observed decrease in the present study. Changes in the size, mobility, dietary habits, and infection burden of the contributing population could also plausibly alter the biological inputs into wastewater; however, corresponding demographic data were not available, and their effects could not be evaluated.Technical factors may also have influenced the observed metagenomic profiles. Although clarification and 0.22 μm filtration were used to reduce intact bacterial cells and larger particulate material, filtration alone cannot eliminate extracellular or particle-protected bacterial nucleic acids remaining in a complex wastewater matrix. In addition, the MgCl2-assisted membrane adsorption and elution procedure was used to concentrate virus-containing material but was not a virus-specific affinity-purification step. Most importantly, total nucleic acid was extracted without DNase treatment, allowing residual bacterial DNA and other unprotected DNA to enter the sequencing libraries. These factors likely contributed to the predominance of bacterial reads (>97%) despite viral enrichment, indicating that the procedure concentrated virus-containing wastewater material rather than producing a purified virome. The persistence of bacterial sequences following virion-enrichment procedures has also been reported in sewage metagenomic studies (Cantalupo et al., 2011). Pretreatment with DNase-based enzymes or Benzonase-containing nuclease cocktails before capsid disruption and nucleic acid extraction has been incorporated into virome-preparation workflows to remove non-particle-protected nucleic acids (Cantalupo et al., 2011; Conceicao-Neto et al., 2015; Brinkman et al., 2018). Database-dependent classification represents an additional source of uncertainty because prophage-related sequences and the incomplete representation of environmental microorganisms and viruses in reference databases may affect individual taxonomic assignments (Cantalupo et al., 2011; Roux et al., 2015; Paez-Espino et al., 2016). Furthermore, while the same general experimental workflow was used across the 3 years, unmeasured variation in transport duration, nucleic acid recovery, or sample-processing and sequencing batches could not be separated from sampling year. Kraken2 was unable to classify 56.42–74.74% of the metagenomic reads at the genus level. This unclassified fraction may contain viral sequences that are highly divergent from existing references or poorly represented in current databases—potentially constituting viral “dark matter”—but may also include sequences of nonviral origin and reads containing insufficient information for reliable classification.Among the bacteriophage communities, taxa represented by the family Fiersviridae exhibited high abundance and stability across different time points. As key members of the Fiersviridae family, F-specific RNA phages stably exist in aquatic environments as potential viral indicators of water pollution (Hata et al., 2016). The persistent presence of the families Astroviridae and Picornaviridae (including enteroviruses and kobuviruses) may reflect widespread community shedding. Conversely, the family Reoviridae and the family Hepeviridae consistently remained at extremely low background levels across all temporal cohorts. Because population-level data on virus-specific infection prevalence and vaccination coverage were unavailable, the low relative abundances observed in wastewater could not be reliably attributed to these factors. Furthermore, given the potential detection biases inherent in metagenomic sequencing of complex wastewater samples, these findings should be interpreted cautiously, as the observed low abundances may partly reflect methodological limitations rather than genuinely low viral abundance. Therefore, in future surveillance, supplementary validation combining highly specific targeted enrichment probes or digital PCR technologies may be required for these low-abundance yet high-risk target viruses, to avoid missing potential sporadic sources of infection.The consistently high abundance of plant-associated viruses in wastewater, particularly the genera Tobamovirus and Potexvirus, is not surprising. Previous studies have demonstrated that plant viruses dominate the viral communities in human fecal samples and are widespread across aquatic biomes (Zhang et al., 2006). Specifically, the genus Tobamovirus primarily originates from the daily human consumption of infected plants and their processed products, which pass through the digestive tract and are excreted in large quantities in feces. Although members of the genus Tobamovirus exhibit strict plant-host specificity, a case–control study reported associations between the detection of pepper mild mottle virus in human stool and specific immune responses and clinical symptoms, including fever, abdominal pain, and pruritus; however, causality was not established (Colson et al., 2010; Editors, 2026). Given its exceptionally high environmental abundance and potential relevance to human health, pepper mild mottle virus warrants consideration for inclusion in environmental surveillance systems. Beyond this, pepper mild mottle virus has been widely validated as an ideal environmental indicator for evaluating the viral removal efficacy of wastewater treatment processes, such as conventional activated sludge and membrane bioreactors (Canh et al., 2025). The high relative abundance of members of the genus Potexvirus in this study is noteworthy. Members of this genus primarily infect herbaceous plants, including many economically important crops. Potato virus X, a representative member of the genus and a member of the species Potexvirus ecspotati, is an important pathogen of potato plants (Verchot, 2022). The frequent detection of potexviruses in wastewater may be associated with the agricultural and dietary context of Gansu Province, where potatoes are extensively cultivated and commonly consumed. Viral particles or nucleic acids originating from infected plant materials may enter municipal wastewater through food processing, food-waste disposal, and excretion following consumption. Sewage pipelines frequently harbor substantial insect populations (Cantalupo et al., 2011), which explains the detection of entomopathogenic viral genera such as Alphanodavirus and Betabaculovirus. In nature, these viruses play an ecological role in regulating insect populations, and certain groups, like baculoviruses, have been developed as microbial control agents (Lacey et al., 2015). full_text_sections.other: IntroductionWastewater-based epidemiology has become a prominent approach to noninvasive public health surveillance, offering a comprehensive snapshot of community-level infectious disease dynamics and environmental health (Crits-Christoph et al., 2021). Driven by advances in high-throughput sequencing, the field has successfully transitioned from targeted PCR assays to untargeted, whole-community metagenomic and metatranscriptomic profiling (Tan et al., 2015). Within municipal wastewater, the virome serves as a critical reservoir of biological information, granting real-time insights into the circulating viruses—including human pathogens, bacteriophages, and diverse environmental viruses—thereby acting as a crucial early warning system for emerging infectious diseases (Rothman et al., 2021). Therefore, profiling of the wastewater virome is imperative for comprehensively assessing viral ecological patterns and population health.Gansu Province, located in northwestern China, serves as an ecologically significant region characterized by a distinct arid climate and unique sociogeographical attributes. Although the region’s resident population reached 24.43 million by the end of 2025, Gansu remains a largely unexplored territory in environmental microbiology despite its profound socioenvironmental significance. To bridge this spatial knowledge gap, this study conducted multiyear wastewater sampling across 6 representative cities. Specifically, raw wastewater samples were collected from wastewater treatment plants in Lanzhou, the provincial capital characterized by high population mobility; Hezuo, which has a multiethnic population; Zhangye, an important transportation hub; Jiuquan and Longnan, which border the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region and Sichuan Province, respectively; and Dingxi, located in central Gansu. The catchment populations served by the sampled wastewater treatment plants exceeded 1 million in Lanzhou and Longnan and 100,000 at each of the other sites. Using high-throughput sequencing, we conducted an exploratory characterization of wastewater viral signals across selected cities in Gansu Province between 2024 and 2026, providing preliminary evidence to support local public health surveillance and targeted decision-making. Collection and processing of the wastewater samplesBetween 2024 and 2026, 18 raw wastewater samples were collected from wastewater treatment plants across 6 cities in Gansu Province (Hezuo, Zhangye, Lanzhou, Jiuquan, Longnan, and Dingxi). Based on their respective sampling years, the samples were categorized into 3 groups: GS24, GS25, and GS26. Seasonal patterns, population differences, and other demographic factors were not considered when defining these groups. Specifically, the sample groups were designated as follows: GS24-1 to GS24-6 were collected in July 2024 from Hezuo, Zhangye, Lanzhou, Jiuquan, Longnan, and Hezuo, respectively; GS25-1 to GS25-6 were collected in June 2025 from Hezuo, Zhangye, Lanzhou, Jiuquan, Longnan, and Zhangye, respectively; and GS26-1 to GS26-6 were collected in March 2026 from Hezuo, Zhangye, Lanzhou, Jiuquan, Longnan, and Dingxi, respectively. GS24-1 and GS24-6 were independently collected on the same day from the same wastewater treatment plant in Hezuo. The same applied to GS25-2 and GS25-6 in Zhangye. The collection dates reflected operational availability and were not selected to provide seasonally matched observations. At each monitoring site, 1 L of raw wastewater was collected. The samples were transported at 4 °C to the laboratory of Gansu Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention within 7 days and processed immediately upon arrival (Wang et al., 2014). For viral concentration, the wastewater samples were initially centrifuged at 1,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C. Subsequently, 2.5 M MgCl2 was added to the supernatant to achieve a final concentration of 0.05 M, and the pH was adjusted to 3.5 using 0.5 N HCl. The prepared solution was then filtered through a 142-mm cellulose nitrate membrane using a positive-pressure pump. Following filtration, the membrane was fragmented and eluted twice with 10 mL of 3% beef extract by vortexing on ice for 5 min each time. The pooled eluates were centrifuged at 1,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C and finally passed through a 0.22 μm syringe filter. Nucleic acid extraction and sequencingTotal nucleic acid extraction was performed using the High Pure Viral Nucleic Acid Kit (Roche) without DNase digestion. To reduce potential false-positive results associated with the increased PCR cycles required for capture-based sequencing, the initial extract was divided for parallel and independent library preparations. Metagenomic libraries were generated with the MGIEasy Fast RNA Library Prep Set, whereas the IGT® Fast Stranded RNA Library Prep Kit v2.0 was applied for capture-based construction. For targeted enrichment, a custom enterovirus probe panel was deployed; this panel was specifically designed for selected viruses, encompassing the species Enterovirus alphacoxsackie, Enterovirus betacoxsackie, Enterovirus coxsackiepol, and Enterovirus deconjuncti. Negative controls were processed in parallel during nucleic acid extraction and library preparation to monitor potential contamination, and no evidence of contamination or other procedural abnormalities was observed. Finally, paired-end reads were generated by sequencing the prepared libraries on a DNBSEQ-T7 platform. Sequence data analysisRaw sequencing reads generated by the metagenomic and targeted-capture workflows were assessed using FastQC1 before downstream analysis. No sequencing dataset was excluded from downstream analysis solely on the basis of the FastQC assessment. For raw paired-end reads, adapter trimming and quality filtering (length <50 bp, quality score <20, or containing N bases) were performed using KneadData.2 High-quality reads were then aligned to the human reference genome (hg19) via Bowtie2 to discard host sequences, with the unmapped reads kept for subsequent analyses (Langmead and Salzberg, 2012). Metagenomic reads were taxonomically classified using Kraken2 across multiple taxonomic levels (Wood et al., 2019). All sequencing reads were assembled using MEGAHIT (Li et al., 2015). Contigs (length ≥300 bp, coverage ≥3×) were filtered via awk and annotated using blastn, taking the highest bitscore as the final assignment (Chen et al., 2015). Read abundances per viral species were quantified using BWA-backtrack for downstream evaluation (Li and Durbin, 2009). All astrovirus- and enterovirus-associated contigs assembled using MEGAHIT were extracted from each sample and individually re-evaluated using NCBI BLASTn.3 Rarefaction analysis and diversity visualizationAll statistical analyses and data visualizations were performed using R 4.4.3 software.4 Specifically, alpha diversity was assessed at the genus level, and the Shannon and inverse Simpson indices were calculated using the vegan package. Hereafter, the term “Simpson index” refers specifically to the inverse Simpson formulation (1/D). Temporal trends in alpha diversity were assessed using one-tailed Spearman’s rank correlation tests, with the a priori hypothesis that diversity indices would decline over sampling years. Spearman’s rho (ρ) values and corresponding one-sided p values were calculated to evaluate the monotonic relationship between sampling year and alpha diversity indices. Rarefaction curves, heatmaps, stacked bar plots, and visualizations of alpha diversity indices were generated using the ggplot2 package. Quantitative profiling of the viromeFor the quantitative analysis of viral communities, relative abundances were estimated using the reads per million normalization method described in Equation 1. The mapped read counts of each viral contig were adjusted for genome length differences by dividing the read counts by the average genome size of the corresponding viral family or genus. title_original: High-throughput sequencing reveals the virome characteristics of wastewater in Gansu Province, China from 2024 to 2026

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the virome of wastewater in Gansu Province, China, from 2024 to 2026, to better understand the presence and diversity of human enteroviruses in this environment. Wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as a valuable tool for monitoring community disease burden.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved collecting 18 raw wastewater samples from six cities in Gansu Province (Hezuo, Zhangye, Lanzhou, Jiuquan, Longnan, and Dingxi) over three years (2024, 2025, and 2026). The samples were categorized into three groups based on their respective sampling years: GS24, GS25, and GS26.
analysis.methods: Wastewater samples were collected between 2024 and 2026 and processed for metagenomic sequencing. The sequencing depth was sufficient to capture most genus-level diversity, as indicated by rarefaction analysis. The data were analyzed using the Shannon and Simpson indices to assess alpha diversity.
analysis.main_results: The Shannon index showed a negative but nonsignificant correlation with sampling year (Spearman’s ρ = −0.354, p = 0.075), while the Simpson index exhibited a significant negative correlation (Spearman’s ρ = −0.472, p = 0.024). More than 97% of the reads were assigned to Bacteria, with no more than 0.94% classified as viral. Additionally, bacteriophages and plant-infecting viruses showed relatively high abundance and consistent detection patterns.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The significant negative correlation between the Simpson index and sampling year suggests that the diversity metrics captured different aspects of community variation. The study highlights the presence of a complex virome with a notable proportion of viral reads attributed to bacteriophages and plant-associated viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the composition and dynamics of the wastewater virome, which can inform surveillance strategies for human enteroviruses. They also emphasize the importance of considering seasonal and environmental factors in virome studies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its small number of annual sampling campaigns conducted in different months, which may affect the interpretation of between-year variation. The dataset is considered an exploratory assessment, and the evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the virome characteristics of wastewater in Gansu Province, China, from 2024 to 2026, focusing on human enteroviruses. Six cities were sampled, yielding 18 wastewater samples divided into three groups based on sampling years. High-throughput sequencing revealed that more than 97% of reads were bacterial, with viral reads comprising no more than 0.94%. The Simpson diversity index showed a significant negative correlation with sampling year, while the Shannon index showed a nonsignificant negative trend. Bacteriophages and plant-infecting viruses were relatively abundant and consistently detected. The study highlights the potential of wastewater-based epidemiology for monitoring human enteroviruses but acknowledges limitations due to the limited number of sampling campaigns and the influence of seasonal factors. The evidence is moderate, as the findings are based on exploratory analyses.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在三年内(2024年、2025年和2026年)收集了甘肃省六个城市(合作、张掖、兰州、酒泉、陇南和定西)的18个原废水样本。样本根据各自的采样年份分为三组:GS24、GS25 和 GS26。
elements_zh.methods: 2024 年至 2026 年间收集废水样本并进行处理以进行宏基因组测序。如稀疏分析所示,测序深度足以捕获大多数属水平的多样性。使用香农和辛普森指数分析数据以评估阿尔法多样性。
elements_zh.main_results: 香农指数与采样年份呈不显着负相关(Spearman’s ρ = -0.354,p = 0.075),而辛普森指数与采样年份呈显着负相关(Spearman’s ρ = -0.472,p = 0.024)。超过 97% 的读数被归为细菌,不超过 0.94% 被归为病毒。此外,噬菌体和感染植物的病毒表现出相对较高的丰度和一致的检测模式。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 辛普森指数和采样年份之间的显着负相关表明多样性指标捕获了群落变化的不同方面。该研究强调了复杂病毒组的存在,其中很大一部分病毒读数归因于噬菌体和植物相关病毒。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了对废水病毒组的组成和动态的深入了解,这可以为 监测 的 监测 策略提供信息。他们还强调在病毒组研究中考虑季节性和环境因素的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其在不同月份进行的年度抽样活动数量较少而受到限制,这可能会影响对年份间变化的解释。该数据集被认为是探索性评估,由于这些限制,证据是中等的。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the virome of wastewater in Gansu Province, China, from 2024 to 2026, to better understand the presence and diversity of human enteroviruses in this environment. Wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as a valuable tool for monitoring community disease burden.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved collecting 18 raw wastewater samples from six cities in Gansu Province (Hezuo, Zhangye, Lanzhou, Jiuquan, Longnan, and Dingxi) over three years (2024, 2025, and 2026). The samples were categorized into three groups based on their respective sampling years: GS24, GS25, and GS26.
analysis_en.methods: Wastewater samples were collected between 2024 and 2026 and processed for metagenomic sequencing. The sequencing depth was sufficient to capture most genus-level diversity, as indicated by rarefaction analysis. The data were analyzed using the Shannon and Simpson indices to assess alpha diversity.
analysis_en.main_results: The Shannon index showed a negative but nonsignificant correlation with sampling year (Spearman’s ρ = −0.354, p = 0.075), while the Simpson index exhibited a significant negative correlation (Spearman’s ρ = −0.472, p = 0.024). More than 97% of the reads were assigned to Bacteria, with no more than 0.94% classified as viral. Additionally, bacteriophages and plant-infecting viruses showed relatively high abundance and consistent detection patterns.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The significant negative correlation between the Simpson index and sampling year suggests that the diversity metrics captured different aspects of community variation. The study highlights the presence of a complex virome with a notable proportion of viral reads attributed to bacteriophages and plant-associated viruses.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the composition and dynamics of the wastewater virome, which can inform surveillance strategies for human enteroviruses. They also emphasize the importance of considering seasonal and environmental factors in virome studies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its small number of annual sampling campaigns conducted in different months, which may affect the interpretation of between-year variation. The dataset is considered an exploratory assessment, and the evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

title_zh: 高通量测序揭示2024至2026年中国甘肃省污水中的病毒组特征
source_body_en: In this study, metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing were employed to preliminarily characterize wastewater viral communities in Gansu Province from 2024 to 2026. In summary, this study provides a preliminary characterization of the viral community profiles in wastewater samples from Gansu Province, demonstrates the effectiveness of wastewater-based epidemiology for population-level surveillance, and underscores the need to establish a coordinated defense network integrating clinical case surveillance with environmental monitoring.Keywords: astroviruses, enterovirus, Gansu Province, metagenomic sequencing, targeted next-generation sequencing, wastewater Materials and methodsCollection and processing of the wastewater samplesBetween 2024 and 2026, 18 raw wastewater samples were collected from wastewater treatment plants across 6 cities in Gansu Province (Hezuo, Zhangye, Lanzhou, Jiuquan, Longnan, and Dingxi). To reduce potential false-positive results associated with the increased PCR cycles required for capture-based sequencing, the initial extract was divided for parallel and independent library preparations. Rarefaction curves, heatmaps, stacked bar plots, and visualizations of alpha diversity indices were generated using the ggplot2 package.Quantitative profiling of the viromeFor the quantitative analysis of viral communities, relative abundances were estimated using the reads per million normalization method described in Equation 1. AbstractEmerging and re-emerging infectious diseases continue to pose a persistent challenge to global public health security. As an unbiased and noninvasive population-level surveillance approach, wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as an urban-scale monitoring tool for proactively capturing the community disease bu...
abstract_zh: 本研究采用宏基因组和靶向下一代测序技术对甘肃省2024年至2026年的废水病毒群落进行了初步表征。总之,本研究提供了甘肃省废水样品中病毒群落特征的初步表征,证明了基于废水的流行病学对人群水平监测的有效性,并强调需要建立结合临床案例监测的协调防御网络关键词: 星状病毒,肠道病毒,甘肃省,宏基因组测序,靶向二代测序,废水 材料与方法 废水样品的采集与处理 2024年至2026年间,从甘肃省6个城市(合作、张掖、兰州、酒泉、陇南、定西)的废水治疗工厂采集了18份原废水样品。为了减少与基于捕获的测序所需的 PCR 循环增加相关的潜在假阳性结果,将初始提取物分为平行和独立的文库制备。使用 ggplot2 包生成稀疏曲线、热图、堆积条形图和 α 多样性指数可视化。病毒组的定量分析为了对病毒群落进行定量分析,使用公式 1 中描述的每百万读数归一化方法估计相对丰度。摘要新出现和重新出现的传染病继续对全球公共卫生安全构成持续挑战。作为一种公正且非侵入性的人群层面的 监测 方法,基于废水的 监测 已成为一种城市规模的监测工具,用于主动捕获社区疾病状况。
summary_zh: 本研究采用宏基因组和靶向下一代测序技术对甘肃省2024年至2026年的废水病毒群落进行了初步表征。总之,本研究提供了甘肃省废水样品中病毒群落特征的初步表征,证明了基于废水的流行病学对人群水平监测的有效性,并强调需要建立结合临床案例监测的协调防御网络关键词: 星状病毒,肠道病毒,甘肃省,宏基因组测序,靶向二代测序,废水 材料与方法 废水样品的采集与处理 2024年至2026年间,从甘肃省6个城市(合作、张掖、兰州、酒泉、陇南、定西)的废水治疗工厂采集了18份原废水样品。为了减少与基于捕获的测序所需的 PCR 循环增加相关的潜在假阳性结果,将初始提取物分为平行和独立的文库制备。使用 ggplot2 包生成稀疏曲线、热图、堆积条形图和 α 多样性指数可视化。病毒组的定量分析为了对病毒群落进行定量分析,使用公式 1 中描述的每百万读数归一化方法估计相对丰度。摘要新出现和重新出现的传染病继续对全球公共卫生安全构成持续挑战。作为一种公正且非侵入性的人群层面的 监测 方法,基于废水的 监测 已成为一种城市规模的监测工具,用于主动捕获社区疾病状况。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在表征 2024 年至 2026 年中国甘肃省废水的病毒组特征,以更好地了解 人肠道病毒 在该环境中的存在和多样性。基于废水的 流行病学 已成为监测社区疾病负担的宝贵工具。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在三年内(2024年、2025年和2026年)收集了甘肃省六个城市(合作、张掖、兰州、酒泉、陇南和定西)的18个原废水样本。样本根据各自的采样年份分为三组:GS24、GS25 和 GS26。
analysis_zh.methods: 2024 年至 2026 年间收集废水样本并进行处理以进行宏基因组测序。如稀疏分析所示,测序深度足以捕获大多数属水平的多样性。使用香农和辛普森指数分析数据以评估阿尔法多样性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 香农指数与采样年份呈不显着负相关(Spearman’s ρ = -0.354,p = 0.075),而辛普森指数与采样年份呈显着负相关(Spearman’s ρ = -0.472,p = 0.024)。超过 97% 的读数被归为细菌,不超过 0.94% 被归为病毒。此外,噬菌体和感染植物的病毒表现出相对较高的丰度和一致的检测模式。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 辛普森指数和采样年份之间的显着负相关表明多样性指标捕获了群落变化的不同方面。该研究强调了复杂病毒组的存在,其中很大一部分病毒读数归因于噬菌体和植物相关病毒。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了对废水病毒组的组成和动态的深入了解,这可以为 监测 的 监测 策略提供信息。他们还强调在病毒组研究中考虑季节性和环境因素的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其在不同月份进行的年度抽样活动数量较少而受到限制,这可能会影响对年份间变化的解释。该数据集被认为是探索性评估,由于这些限制,证据是中等的。
